subject: Cooking
title: Fat Doesn't Make You Fat
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fat Doesn't Make You Fat.

hook.text: For decades, 'low-fat' was the holy grail of healthy eating. Obesity rates doubled during the low-fat era.

buildup.text: In 1977, the US government advised Americans to cut fat. Food companies replaced fat with sugar.

discovery.text: Excess calories from any source — carbs, protein, or fat — cause weight gain. Fat itself isn't uniquely fattening.

twist.text: Low-fat products often contain more sugar and calories than their full-fat counterparts.

climax.text: Healthy fats (olive oil, avocados, nuts) are now recognized as essential and even protective against heart disease.

punchline.text: The 'low-fat' era didn't make us thinner. It made us sweeter.

quiz.question: What did food companies often add when they removed fat from products?

details.summary: Eating fat does not directly cause body fat gain — excess calories from any source do. The low-fat diet craze of the 1980s and 1990s replaced fat with sugar and refined carbs, contributing to rising obesity. Healthy fats from nuts, avocados, and olive oil are now considered essential.
details.whyItMatters: The anti-fat movement led to decades of misguided dietary advice and products loaded with sugar to compensate. Understanding fat's role corrects one of nutrition's most damaging myths.
takeaways: Total calorie balance determines weight gain, not fat consumption alone
Low-fat products often contain more sugar to maintain palatability
Healthy fats support hormone production and nutrient absorption

faq.question: Why did we believe fat was the enemy?
faq.answer: Influential but flawed studies in the 1960s linked dietary fat to heart disease. The food industry lobbied to shift blame from sugar to fat. Government guidelines promoted low-fat diets for decades. Sugar industry documents revealed deliberate efforts to downplay sugar's health risks.

faq.question: Which fats are actually unhealthy?
faq.answer: Trans fats from partially hydrogenated oils are genuinely harmful and now largely banned. Excessive saturated fat from processed foods may raise health risks. But unsaturated fats from olive oil, nuts, fish, and avocados are protective and essential for health.
